rv.q: Kessler’s play is certainly a springboard for actors, but for audiences, it sags and slumps.
Too often, Forbes Masson’s Harold veers from magical realism into caricature, an avuncular take on a mafia boss.
Unfortunately however, in Treat’s case, the clothes do not make the man and his character struggles to rise above his historical personality failings.
It’s darkly funny and emotionally bruising and well worth catching.
Despite some good performances and American accents from the three actors, by the end we could not care less whether they live or die.

cn.t: Strong performances, particularly from the leads, elevate this 1983 drama, but the production struggles with uneven pacing and unclear character motivations that leave critics divided on its overall impact.
